play_source_comment: Oil charge from KCF source is proven in The Eocene of the area.  It is possible that the Fulmar may also access the Central Graben mature KCF, as seen further north in the Greater Kittiwake area.
play_reservoir_comment: Fulmar sandstone is know from the Western Platform to be typically located in interpods from well and supported by seismic data.  In the immediate area sandstone is proven from well penetrations, though this is typically thin and the distribution patchy.
play_seal_comment: Where KCF is thin or absent, the overlying Lower Cretaceous Cromer Knoll marls will provide a top seal.
source_presence_comment: Oil charge from KCF source is proven in the area.
source_effectiveness_comment: Requires migration within Fulmar sandstone in interpods linking into the Central Graben.  The interpod linkage seems likely from seismic, however, Fulmar sandstone distribution may be patchy.
reservoir_presence_comment: Thin Fulmar sandstone is known from offset wells, often argillaceous with patchy distribution.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Relatively shallowly buried, however, offset wells indicate that primary reservoir quality can be an issue in the area.
trap_presence_comment: Three way dip closure with lateral seal against a Smith Bank Mudstone pod is mappable on seismic.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Requires seal against Smith Bank mudstone; this is a well known proven trap type.
geophysical_cos_comment: No modifier used.

play_source_comment: The oil accumulations at Buzzard, Ettrick, Blackbird, Polecat and Marten strongly imply an effective source and kitchen area was present in the Ettrick Graben nearby the Tybalt prospect. In addition to this, source rock modelling suggests that the KCF source rocks present in the nearby offset wells lies within the upper portion of the oil window within the Tybalt Prospect area.
play_reservoir_comment: Relies on the presence of Buzzard reservoirs likely to be at deeper stratigraphic levels to those encountered in the 20/7-2 well and is based on a seismically defined isochron that thickens into the prospect area from the wells drilled in the Tybalt Half-Graben including 20/7-2. Nevertheless, regional correlation to the Blackbird area suggests this could be the case. Reservoir quality expected to be good.
play_seal_comment: Top seals formed by the KCF form the top seals for several oil accumulations in the area and so are considered to have a very high chance to be present.
source_presence_comment: The KCF is well developed in all the surrounding wells (eg 20/2-1), with high TOC and oil-prone kerogen. Discoveries to the north prove the Ettrick Graben as an oil kitchen, but migration to Tybalt has some risk. The Tybalt half-graben itself may be oil-generative (shows in 20/7-2 etc) but nearby dry holes highlight the risk. The KCF within much of the Tybalt half-graben is also buried deeper than the 10300 ft depth to onset of oil expulsion.
source_effectiveness_comment: The presence of an effective oil migration pathway is de-risked to some extent by oil shows in the 20/7-2 well. However, because oil is required to migrate laterally from the thicker parts of the Ettrick Graben further northeast, then this remains a risk, unless in situ generation has occurred.  The structuration that occurred prior to the Cretaceous gave rise to much of the trap geometry and so was in existence during the time of oil expulsion and migration.
reservoir_presence_comment: The presence of lower Buzzard reservoirs deeper than those penetrated in 20/7-2 is a risk for the prospect and is based on a seismically defined isochron that thickens into the prospect area.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Offset well data indicates that reservoir quality at this depth is not a significant risk. Average porosity in the Buzzard sandstones of 20/7a-4 is 21%. Based on core porosity-k relationships this should equate to average permeabilities of several hundred mD or more and multi-D permeabilities are quite common in Buzzard sandstones.
trap_presence_comment: Combination of two-way dip closure in the footwall of the Blackbird Fault and a southwestward up-dip stratigraphic termination of lower Buzzard reservoirs. The structural component of the trap is defined by 3D seismic data and is reliable in this area. The stratigraphic trap component is also seen from seismic data but the extent to which it contains terminations of sandstone units is based on regional considerations in combination with the eastward thickening seismic isochron.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Buzzard field is an excellent analogue as it involves up-dip pinch out of reservoir units towards the west, dip closure to the east and downside fault closure to north and south. Top seal is provided by KCF shales and bottom seal is provided by KCF and Heather Fm shales. Maximum flooding surfaces separating the sandstone units commonly act as pressure seals.
geophysical_cos_comment: X-plot shows fairly good relationship between seismic isochron and sandstone reservoir thickness for Ettrick and Buzzard sandstones, which is a helpful predictive tool.

trap_presence_comment: The trap is formed by a combination of two-way dip closure in the footwall area of a northwest dipping normal fault and a northwestward up-dip stratigraphic termination of Jurassic sandstone reservoirs. The structural component of the trap is defined by 3D seismic data and is reliable in this area. The stratigraphic trap component is also seen but the extent to which it contains terminations of sandstone units is based on regional considerations in combination with the thickening isochron.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The stratigraphic component is defined locally to some extent on its southern margin where Ettrick or Buzzard Sandstones are absent in the 20/8-1 well. Buzzard field is an excellent analogue for the strat component as it involves up-dip pinch out of reservoir units towards the west. Top seal is provided by KCF shales and bottom seal is provided by KCF and Heather Fm shales. Maximum flooding surfaces separating the sandstone units commonly act as pressure seals.
geophysical_cos_comment: X-plot shows fairly good relationship between seismic isochron and sandstone reservoir thickness for Ettrick and Buzzard sandstones, which is a helpful predictive tool.

play_source_comment: The presence of oil and oil shows in the 20/8-2 well demonstrates an oil migration pathway into part of the prospect area, even though the source of oil migration is unknown, either being from the Ettrick Graben or Peterhead Graben. Minor oil shows in the Piper Formation in well 20/8-1, and in the Zechstein section in well 20/9-1 also provide evidence of oil migration into the area. The 20/8-2 oil is derived from an early mature source.
play_reservoir_comment: The play involves the presence of Ettrick and/or Buzzard reservoirs surrounding the 20/8-2 well, and continuation of sandstones towards the 20/8-1 well. The presence of Upper Jurassic sandstones nearby 20/8-1 is interpreted from the marked thickening of the equivalent seismic isochron just a short distance from the well.
play_seal_comment: The KCF forms the top seals for several oil accumulations in the area and so seals are considered to have a very high chance to be present.

The oil shows in the 20/7b-5 well may support the Peterhead Graben as a potential source kitchen for the 20/8-2 well and the Tempest prospect. reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Tay sands in the downdip 22/26a-1 well (1.5 km away) have excellent reservoir properties.
trap_presence_comment: The Tay is draped over the diapir and has a sound trapping geometry although whether the reservoir extends to the south of the diapir would affect whether it is a 3 or 4 way dipping geometry.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The thick succession of Horda shales would provide competent seal capabilities above the Tay and is a reliable seal in the region. An element of side seal is required by the diapir which should itself be impermeable but there is the risk that permeable stratigraphy caught in the diapir walls could transport hydrocarbons ?around? the top seal.
geophysical_cos_comment: No visible anomaly on diapir flank or close to base

Otherwise commercial discoveries are present in multiple diapir based prospects in the area including Banff (15km away) and Kyle (16km away) where commercial levels of hydrocarbons migrated into the trap.
reservoir_presence_comment: he Upper Cretaceous Chalks were deposited as pelagic ooze which was subsequently re-worked and went through a complex diagenetic history. trap_effectiveness_comment: The carbonates of the chalk group can be highly diverse with carbonates capable of acting as both reservoir and seal. Otherwise the Sele Formation and Horda shales would provide reliable sealing components. An element of side seal is required by the diapir. Likely to forma continuous column with the Forties Sandstone Member.

reservoir_presence_comment: Seismic geometry suggests the Duncansby reservoir may have been sourced from the Canary High. Sand presence is only inferred by the interpretation of fan-like geometry on seismic, so some risk to sand presence is carried.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Effective reservoir remains a risk within this depositional setting where early diagenetic processes could occlude porosity soon after burial, and possibly before charge (note that much of the cored Claymore sand in wells 14/20b-23 and -30 has permeability <1mD).
trap_presence_comment: Trap geometry has some uncertainty and there is risk of failure where the inferred sands may be juxtaposed with the Lowlander-Canary High bounding fault.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Some seal against the Canary High may be necessary, suggesting that the Claymore could be juxtaposed against Carboniferous and the Lowlander bounding fault. The fact that Lowlander is not full to spill suggests that some sort of leak is occurring along this fault. Seismic indicates that chance of leak from this sand lobe into another Claymore lobe is quite high.

source_effectiveness_comment: Holborn is immediately downdip of well 14/20b-30 which encountered good oil shows in the Claymore Member. The source and short migration path that are proven in the Chanonry 14/20b-24 well are envisaged for this prospect.

trap_presence_comment: The Holborn prospect relies on updip seal against the Carboniferous of the Claymore-Highlander Ridge, but in all other aspects is a stratigraphic trap. In places the prospect is overlain by other Claymore Sandstone bodies such as the Duncansby prospect. Seismic inversion is essential to aid the understanding of the potentially complex interplay of various Claymore Member packages and trap.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Trap geometry has some uncertainty and there is risk of trap failure where the inferred sands appear to be juxtaposed with Carboniferous sands at the Claymore-Highlander ridge.Like the Duncansby and Lismore prospects there is potential for lack of separation between Claymore Member bodies.

play_source_comment: A working hydrocarbon system is proven by producing fields to the north-east, east and south. The Westphalian succession is proven as an excellent dry gas source. Well and seismic data suggest that the Westphalian subcrops in most parts of the application area.
play_reservoir_comment: All surrounding wells have encountered Leman reservoir aside from well 42/27a-1, which may have been located on a stable platform high during deposition.
play_seal_lithology: Mudstone of the Silverpit/Evaporites & carbonates of the Zechstein
play_seal_comment: The Silverpit Fm and overlying Zechstein Gp provide top seal to the Lower Leman Sandstone at local discoveries. The Silverpit Fm is present at most local wells although is absent to the west of the application block at well 42/26-1. Post deposition of the Silverpit the entire Southern Permian Basin was inundated by the transgression of the Zechstein Sea which resulted in deposition of evaporites and carbonates. Many local wells do not have indications of hydrocarbon presence above the Zechstein.
source_presence_comment: A working hydrocarbon system is proven by producing fields to the north-east, east and south. Seismic and well data suggest that Earn is underlain by Carboniferous rocks. It is difficult to determine with the current dataset as to the precise age of these although it is estimated that they date mostly from the Westphalian.
source_effectiveness_comment: Minor risk that the underlying Westphalian is of Namurian age and/or sub-parallel to the Top Rotliegendes which may be sub-optimal for migration.In addition, there is a risk that the Carboniferous subcrop geometry may direct gas away from Earn.
reservoir_presence_comment: All surrounding wells have encountered Leman reservoir aside from well 42/27a-1, which may have been located on a stable platform high during deposition. Perhaps the best well analogue in terms of Rotliegendes seismic stratigraphy for Earn is well 42/27a-3. This encountered an Upper and Lower Leman Sandstone, with net to gross of 53% and average porosity of 15%.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Earn is located on the edge of the basin where the chance of encountering relatively poor-quality fluvial facies down-dip is high.Field reservoir analogues for Earn include Mongour, York, Tolmount,Tolmount E,Artemis & Cleeton. The average NTG among these is 68%, while porosity averages at 15.8% and gas saturation at 64%.Illite cementation is considered unlikely given the relative proximity of Tolmount which lacks an abundance of this type of cement and likely shares a similar structural history.
trap_presence_comment: Earn is a dip and fault closed structure with a crest at ~2945m TVDSS. There is generally good pick confidence in the Top Rotliegendes TWT horizon over Earn, although over the crest seismic noise results in moderate confidence. The base reservoir pick is defined by the BPU which has moderate to low interpretation confidence. Depth conversion uncertainty is significant at Earn given rapid thickness changes, in what is sometimes, a difficult to interpret overburden.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The Silverpit Formation and/or Zechstein Group provide top seal and lateral seal for Earn. The faults which Earn relies on for seal are generally well imaged on seismic aside from where throws are relatively low. In places there is some evidence for Rotliegendes on Rotliegendes juxtaposition which increases the risk of breach of seal. However, the intra Leman shale which separates the Upper and Lower units may work as an effective clay smear helping to seal these faults.

Well 42/27a-3 to the west of the prospect had gas shows in the Rotliegendes and Carboniferous. Hence risks associated with source and migration are thought to be minimal at Tummel.
source_effectiveness_comment: The geometry of the Carboniferous underlying Tummel appears to be sub-parallel to the Top Rotliegendes horizon, although better seismic imaging is needed in-order to prove this. This may mean that migration pathways are more tortuous than if angular discordance between the Carboniferous and Permian existed.
reservoir_presence_comment: Well and seismic data suggest Tummel should have both Upper and Lower Leman sandstone reservoir, although perhaps not so thick as Earn.  A reservoir thickness range of 40 to 60m has been modelled in the volumetrics for Tummel.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Palaeogeographic maps suggest the Tummel reservoir consists of a mixed aeolian-fluvial signature. It is also likely that a higher percentage of fluvial facies is present than at Earn, meaning reservoir quality at this prospect could be poorer.  This is reflected in a slightly lower NTG range than Earn (50-60-75%). Tummel is likely to have had a similar structural history to Tolmount and hence illite cementation is thought not to be dominant.
trap_presence_comment: Although the trap currently covers blocks 47/2b&3g there is some uncertainty in the position of the bounding fault meaning it could be possible that updip sections of the prospect may extend into block 42/28g. The bounding fault at Tummel is clearly imaged aside from at the western limit; where several faults merge.There is less overburden thickness variability than Earn but still some potential for various depth conversion methodologies to result in significant changes to trap geometry.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Top and lateral seal are provided by the Silverpit Fm and/or Zechstein Gp. The thickness of the Zechstein Gp is similar at Earn and Tummel to that at Tolmount. Tummel relies on up-dip fault seal with the reservoir being mostly juxtaposed against the Zechstein Gp. However, in places Rotliegendes on Rotliegendes juxtaposition is possible. While this is a risk for trap integrity it is possible that the intra Leman shale works as an effective fault plane clay smear.

reservoir_presence_comment: The character of the seismic stratigraphy of the Rotliegendes at Earn North is similar to that at well 42/27b-2. Hence the most likely scenario is Upper and Lower Leman sandstone reservoirs being present.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Average Rotliegendes thickness over Earn N is 90m which corresponds to 40m of Leman reservoir. trap_presence_comment: There is some potential for various depth conversion methodologies to result in significant changes to trap geometry.The Top Rotliegendes and BPU reflectors are less coherent over Earn N and more difficult to map than over Earn meaning less confidence is had in trap geometry. Most of the faults at Earn N are imaged well although the southern most fault which trends approximately west to east is of limited throw and consequently imaging is challenging.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Top Zechstein is considerably thinner over Earn N than Earn, Tummel and Tolmount. There is evidence of oil shows above the Zechstein in the Wroot Fm at local well 42/27b-2 (likely water bearing Leman) which is adjacent to faults which cut through the Zechstein into the post salt. A sample of this oil was not retrieved and so it is uncertain as to whether it has a pre or post salt origin. This has implications for Earn N in that it raises the risk of a breached top seal being present.

Therefore there is some potential for various depth conversion methodologies to result in significant changes to trap geometry.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Palaeogeographic maps suggest the Silverpit Fm is present above Belivat. The Zechstein Gp is relatively thin above Belivat and in-fact there is evidence of sub-salt faults cutting through the Zechstein into the post salt overburden. Despite this, wells with hydrocarbon shows above the Zechstein are rare.

The prospect is likely underlain by rocks of Westphalian age, unlike the Rotliegendes at wells 42/27a-1 and 3 which were drilled into a separate upthrown block. source_effectiveness_comment: Doine is located downdip of a gas discovery, within the Carboniferous, at well 42/27a-1. reservoir_effectiveness_comm: If the Upper Leman is present it is likely to be dominated by fluvial facies. Seismic inversion and improved imaging may help to reduce reservoir presence uncertainty. trap_presence_comment: The trap is defined as a structural closure reliant on fault seal to the south and west with dip closure elsewhere. Pick certainty at Top Rotliegendes and BPU is moderate to high. Imaging of the western bounding fault is good while that of the southern is moderate to good. There is some potential for various depth conversion methodologies to result in significant changes to trap geometry especially given the current relatively low structural height of the trap.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Palaeogeographic mapping suggests Silverpit is present at Doine. Ultimately the top seal for this prospect could be the Zechstein Gp. The southern bounding fault juxtaposes the reservoir against the Millstone Grit which was penetrated updip at well 42/27a-1. This well encountered a mudstone rich interval with interbeds of sandstone with gas shows (15-30ft thick). This suggests that there is a high magnitude of uncertainty associated with the sealing capacity of the Doine southern bounding fault.

Confidence in most of the mapped faults is high although the eastern most bounding faults carry only moderate confidence due to seismic noise.

play_source_comment: Westphalian A-B Coal Measures are regionally proven world class source rocks; maturity and migration are supported by our 3D basin model. The Scremerston source rock is a regionally proven source rock.
play_reservoir_comment: Regional indications from our Play Based Exploration for good reservoir quality (e.g. at Endeavour and Kirkleatham) and building on analogue carbonate fields along the rims of the Southern Permian basin in e.g. onshore the Netherlands and Germany.
play_seal_comment: Regionally proven high-quality top seal. Proven at e.g. Crosgan, Breagh and many other fields towards the southeast.
source_presence_comment: Westphalian is not expected to be present in the blocks, but deeper Carboniferous source rocks are expected (Scremerston). Maturity to be further assessed by fine-tuning our recent existing basin model.
source_effectiveness_comment: Access to charge either direct from Scremerston shales or longer migration pathways are possible, but to be refined by dedicated fine-tuning of our recent 3D basin model.
reservoir_presence_comment: Drilled hole analysis and seismic analysis in the area confirms presence of the Zechstein Z3 Plattendolomite, incl. 41/5-1, 41/15-1, 41/20-1, 41/24-1 (Endeavour) and 41/25-1.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The mapped reservoir structures within the blocks indicate different seismic facies compared to well 41/15-1 with tight reservoir, suggesting better reservoir quality.
trap_presence_comment: Structuration has been mapped on 2D seismic.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Evaporitic sections of the Zechstein overlying the reservoir structures have been identified on the 2D seismic (soft acoustic impedance) within the blocks. The effectiveness is uncertain in this area, related to limited thickness and potential faulting, causing leak paths.
geophysical_cos_comment: At this play level no geophysical evidence has been identified to date. Due to the heterogeneous character of carbonate reservoirs (depositional and diagenetically) the expectation for DHI support is low.

play_source_comment: Source rock presence and effectiveness and charge to the eastern flank of the Foula Basin is proven by nearby wells and fields: Clair, Edradour, Glendronach, 206/12-2. 206/11-1, 206/4-1.  Additionally 65m of the Upper Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Fm was encountered at the Bunnehaven discovery (214/9-1).
play_reservoir_comment: Proven by nearby wells 206/4-1, 206-3-1, 206/15-1, 206/4-2 (Edradour), 206/4a-4 (Glendronach).
play_seal_comment: A number of Cretaceous discoveries and sealed by both intraformational (Edradour & 206/4-1 gas pays) and Top Sealing shale facies (Glendronach, 206/12-2, 206/8-4),
source_presence_comment: MacBeth sits on the flank of the Rona Ridge located between the Clair field and the likely kitchen for this accumulation. There is a high chance of working kitchen to charge this feature.
source_effectiveness_comment: The 205/15-1 well is downdip of MacBeth and the MacBeth sandstones had gas shows at this location. The target is located beneath the ultimate top-seal for the Cretaceous objectives and is in a good position for migration
reservoir_presence_comment: The target package is associated with an isopach thick and a bright amplitude response both of which might suggest the presence of sand in a fan qeometry. The package is located down dip of a Cretaceous entry point which cuts back into the Rona Ridge. At the erosional limit of this entry point, well 206/12-2 penetrated 32m of Lower Cretaceous sands.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Reservoir quality is identified as a key risk for this lead. The nearby 205/15-1 contained a MacBeth interval sandstones which had an average porosity of 12%. However the lead is shallower than this and so an improved reservoir quality is expected if the facies is developed
trap_presence_comment: The trap is mapped on 3D as a 3 way roll with updip pinch out and fault control. Up-dip trap is identified as a key risk in the prospect due to the complexity of the faulting system which controls the up-dip extent of the package and its interplay with the target interval.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The MacBeth formation is overlain by the regional Top seal which should be robust. Cross fault seal is a risk as fault throw varies along strike.

play_source_comment: Source rock presence and effectiveness is proven by nearby wells and fields: Glenrothes (208/11-1), Cragganmore (208/17-3), Tobermory (214/4-1), 208/19-1 and Bunnehaven (214/9-1). 65m of the Upper Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Fm was encountered at the Bunnehaven discovery (214/9-1).
play_reservoir_comment: Proven by nearby well Bunnehaven (214/9-1). Moderate gas shows were recorded in the Turonian sands of the Bunnehaven well (214/9-1).
play_seal_comment: The Bunnehaven well, 214/9-1 encountered a thick section of Late Cretaceous mudstones which could act as top seal for the prospect.
source_presence_comment: 65m of the Upper Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Fm was encountered at the 214/9-1, Bunnehaven field (19km south).
source_effectiveness_comment: There is seismic evidence of gas immediately up-dip (at Tobermory) and above the Dun Telve Cretaceous trap. Also, Moderate gas shows were encountered in Turonian age sandstones at the Bunnehaven well, 214/9-1 (19km south), thus proving source effectiveness and migration into the Turonian.
reservoir_presence_comment: At the Dun Telve Cretaceous prospect reservoir presence and quality are significant risks. Well control for the Cretaceous is difficult as many of the surrounding wells targeted shallower prospects and typically TD?d before the Cretaceous. However, the nearest well 214/9-1 (Bunnehaven) penetrated a Turonian section with gas shows. The prospect is not fully covered by existing 3D datasets, with some mapping having to be completed on 2D data. This leaves some reservoir presence uncertainty.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: 214/9-1 (Bunnehaven) penetrated a Turonian section which was tight, with relatively low porosity. A higher amplitude seismic package at the prospect compared to 214/9-1 may indicate better quality sands. Cretaceous reservoir distributions suggest that the prospect sits in a more proximal location then 214/9-1, thus potentially improving reservoir quality. The prospect is not fully covered by existing 3D, with some mapping completed on 2D data, which leaves some reservoir quality uncertainty.
trap_presence_comment: The trap is not fully covered by existing 3D datasets, with some mapping having to be completed on 2D data. This leaves some trap geometry uncertainty.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The Bunnehaven well, 214/9-1 encountered a thick section of Cretaceous mudstones which could act as top seal for the prospect. Lateral up-dip fault seal may work given the mud dominated Cretaceous section encountered at 214/9-1. A large risk for the prospect is that if the trap relies on fault seal there is a risk of leakage, via faults with relatively small throw towards a high with greater topographic relief beneath Tobermory.

play_source_comment: Source rock presence and effectiveness is proven by nearby wells and fields: Glenrothes (208/11-1), Cragganmore (208/17-3), Tobermory (214/4-1), 208/19-1 and Bunnehaven (214/9-1). 65m of the Upper Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Fm was encountered at the Bunnehaven discovery (214/9-1).
play_reservoir_comment: The Vaila reservoir is proven by nearby wells and fields - Glenrothes (208/11-1), Cragganmore (208/17-3), 208/19-1, Glenlivet and Laggan. Well 208/17-2 was P&A as dry but had gas shows in the Lamba T38 and the Vaila, this could be a similar situation to the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect.
play_seal_lithology: Intraformational mudstones/shales of the Vaila/Lamba or the Kettla Tuff
play_seal_comment: Intraformational Vaila shale seals are proven by nearby wells - Glenrothes (208/11-1), Cragganmore (208/17-3) and 208/19-1. In 214/28-1 the Westerhouse Sandstone Mbr of the Lamba Fm was encountered, along with a thick sequence of overlying mudstone. These mudstones could provide an effective top seal for the Lamba section in the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect. Top seal is also present in the form of the overlying Kettla Tuff.
source_presence_comment: 65m of the Upper Jurassic Kimmeridge Clay Fm was encountered at the 214/9-1, Bunnehaven discovery (20km south).
source_effectiveness_comment: Source and migration for the prospect carries little risk as there is seismic evidence of gas immediately up-dip (at Tobermory), also there is a gas column present in the Palaeocene at Bunnehaven (214/9-1). The seismic suggests the presence of faults which could provide direct migration pathways from the Jurassic into the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect.
reservoir_presence_comment: The most significant risk for the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect is reservoir presence and quality. However, this may have more to do with the lack of well penetrations and information on the Vaila/Lamba Fms in this area of the WOS. There is potential for Greenland sourced basin and slope fans for the Vaila (Jolley et al., 2005), placing the prospect in a proximal position.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The most significant risk for the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect is reservoir presence and quality. However, this may have more to do with the lack of well penetrations and information on the Vaila/Lamba Fms in this area of the WOS. Encouraging work has been completed that suggests that reservoir quality rocks could be present in this area of the WOS (Morton et al., 2002; Jolley et al., 2005).
trap_presence_comment: Defining trap geometry for the Dun Telve Palaeocene prospect is complicated by the presence of a significant thickness of volcanics. This hindering of delineation of the trap represents a small risk for the prospect. However, the top surface of the basalt provides some guidance on the underlying structure of the Vaila and/or Lamba interval. The down-dip section of the prospect is not fully covered by 2D/3D data.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The seal for this prospect is probably intraformational shales and mudstones of the Vaila/Lamba. There is also potential for volcanic submarine flow units (or lavas) and hyaloclastites to be sealing. The seismic suggests a thick sequence of basalt could act as top seal. There appear to be faults that crosscut the reservoir into the overburden, which could act as a potential leak point, therefore increasing the seal risk. There are also gas clouds present above the reservoir.

trap_effectiveness_comment: Seal has been highlighted as one of the main risks for the prospect. play_source_comment: The Kimmeridge Clay Formation (KCF) has been penetrated throughout West of Shetlands; mature oil-prone source facies are established within the proximal Faroe-Shetland and Solan Basins. The KCF of these basins onlap onto the Rona Ridge, providing a suitable migration pathway, as proven by the Lancaster Field and Lincoln accumulation
play_reservoir_comment: The Rona Ridge is composed of naturally fractured Lewisian Gneiss which comprises tonalite with subordinate dolerite and basalt. Commercial rates from this formation have been demonstrated at the Lancaster Field and Lincoln Crestal well (205/26b-14)
play_seal_comment: Regional thick interval of Upper Cretaceous mudstones dominated by the Kyrre and Jorsalfare Formations, which provide an extensive and robust top and lateral seal over Lincoln and at the Lancaster and Clare Fields. In addition, the onlap of Upper Jurassic claystones (Kimmeridge Clay Formation) contributes to the seal locally.
source_presence_comment: Source maturity of the Faroe-Shetland Basin has been confirmed by discoveries at Foinaven, Schiehallion, Lancaster and the Clare Field. Mature oil-prone KCF source rock has been proven in proximity to the 205/26f block; offset wells of 205/26-1 and those of the Solan Field demonstrate typical TOC richness between 4-10 wt.%, peaking at 15.4 wt.%. KCF of the Solan Basins, at present day, remain within the oil window, where thicknesses of around 60 m (205/26a-3 well) have been penetrated
source_effectiveness_comment: Hydrocarbons have been proven at Lincoln and the Solan/Strathmore fields, demonstrating the effectiveness of the local KCF source in migration and timing. Migration pathways are primarily from the KCF source horizons directly into the reservoir, hence minimal migration distance
reservoir_presence_comment: The reservoir has been intensely faulted and fractured over 2.7 billion years. Presence and effectiveness of faults and fractures in the reservoir has been proven in the Lancaster and Lincoln accumulations (also Clare Field). This reservoir is a 'type 1 fractured reservoir', where there is little to no matrix porosity or permeability. The effective reservoir is provided by a pervasive fault and fracture network. Faults are seismically resolveable and mappable on specially reprocessed volumes.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The fractured basement reservoir, at the Lincoln Crestal well (205/26b-14), has proven to flow hydrocarbons to surface at commercial rates of 9,800 BOPD during DST. Reservoir effectiveness is analogous to the Lancaster field; however the fracture network might change away from well control
trap_presence_comment: 'Buried Hill' trap presence is proven in the Lincoln Crestal well (205/26b-14) within a local four-way dip closure clearly defined on PSDM 3D seismic. Trap presence is interpreted to maintain effectiveness below local structural closure, as demonstrated by well 205/26b-12 through a combination of gas chromatography,  gas isotope analysis, shows in SWCs, NMR fluid response and oil extracts from cuttings, to determine OWC depths within a fault bounded 3 way dip closure
trap_effectiveness_comment: Local trap effectiveness has been proven in the Lincoln Crestal well (205/26b-14) and 205/26b-12 well. Light undegraded oil has either inferred from geological and wireline data or extracted during drill stem testing. Local Rona Sandstone onlaps could contribute to the HC column, however, top seal at this location could be compromised by fault breach of the KCF and Cretaceous mud rock seal
geophysical_cos_comment: Overall chance of success remains the same as the structure has been defined using 3D seismic volumes and attributes
well_location_cos_comment: Overall chance of success remains the same as the Lincoln structure has already been penetrated by two fractured basement targeted wells (205/26b-12 and 205/26b-14)

play_source_comment: The Kimmeridge Clay is a prolific source rock in the Central North Sea and is widely accepted to be the main source interval for hydrocarbon fields in the play area.

source_presence_comment: The presence of hydrocarbons in wells on the crest of the Helios structure demonstrates source presence and maturity.

play_source_comment: Proven Rotliegend play concept in the Southern North Sea
play_reservoir_comment: The northernmost occurrence of the Rotliegend as a reservoir is in the Auk field in Block 30/16. However, there is a recurrence of the Rotliegend sandstone in the Moray Firth at the Blake field in well 13/24-4. While the depth of burial in the Central Graben makes it beyond the range of most existing wells, where it becomes uplifted it is often eroded.
play_seal_comment: Proven effective seal from many wells off the UKCS
source_presence_comment:
Sourcing of hydrocarbons from basinward juxtaposition with Kimmeridgian source rocks would be problematic,
but cannot be ruled out; however, the local presence of Carboniferous source rocks, if proven, would greatly
increase the chance of charging the structure, thus inheriting a similar play concept to Carboniferous sourced Southern North Sea fields.
source_effectiveness_comment: Source effectiveness is a key risk and would be the focus of the work program to mature Frollo South into a drill-worthy prospect due to lack of analogous fields nearby however the Auk field in 30/16 proves that the play can succeed.
reservoir_presence_comment: A nearby well 22/23b-4R01 drilled into the top of the Rotliegend and TD?ed after drilling 197 feet of 100% sand with average 14% porosity, but failed to measure any pressures and therefore it is assumed to be tight.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm:
Although nearby well 22/23b-4R01 was assumed tight, better seismic facies can be seen down-thrown from this structure, which may indicate a better reservoir facies
and a more complete section of Upper Rotliegend could be present.
trap_presence_comment:
The Lead is fault-closed principally in 3 directions: to the
north against a large east-west fault separating the structure from Frollo North, and this fault is
connected to two large NNW-SSE faults which bound the structure to the east and west, as shown on the Base
Zechstein / Top Rotliegend depth map and the east-west seismic and geoseismic lines.
trap_effectiveness_comment:
The Rotliegend objective is characterised by a thick package of high amplitude reflectivity suggesting possible
multiple reservoir seal pairs.

source_presence_comment: Regionally pervasive and proven by offset wells with multiple hydrocarbon accumulations at multiple stratigraphic levels. The Kimmeridge Clay Fm. has been proven a mature and viable source for established surrounding fields in the Mesozoic and Paleocene.
source_effectiveness_comment: Proven by HC migration into other Tertiary fields and discoveries in the NNS e.g. Nuggets. Vertical migration through faults and fractures from the Jurassic and Triassic reservoirs is evident in the form the gas chimneys on seismic sections and oil stains or shows in well cuttings throughout the Cretaceous and early Paleocene. Lateral migration routes through Paleocene sands are also visible on the spectral decomposition maps.
reservoir_presence_comment: The Asagao and Asagao North prospects exhibit clear differential compaction and channelised geometries, implying a high energy environment depositing unconsolidated, high porosity, sands.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Sand bypass and shale interbeds are also possible and may provide vertical and lateral compartmentalisation. Secondary mineralisation, particularly of glauconite, and other diagenetic processes may cause a reduction in porosity and permeability.
trap_presence_comment: A clear four-way dip closure exists across the Asagao prospect is clearly evident and is defined in both time and depth. A similar, but less regular, four-way dip closure also traps Asagao North. Some stratigraphic trapping may also be considered especially up-dip towards the shelf edge, where the sediment entry input point is located and a pinch-out geometry is assumed. A small NE-SW fault along Asagao?s SE edge may also provide a localised fault trap.
trap_effectiveness_comment: A regional and massive shale succession, in excess of 1000ft thickness, is present in 3/15-5 and 3/15-6 and can be seismically mapped and correlated between these two wells and over Asagao and Asagao North.
geophysical_cos_comment: SAAM DHI Boost of 44%

play_source_comment: The Westphalian Coal Measures of the Carboniferous are the extensive primary source rocks for gas fields in the SNS. The coals, which are deeply buried in fluvial-deltaic sediments, are within the gas window of the source kitchen and have charged many of the SNS reservoirs. Multiple wells have penetrated the Carboniferous interval in the SNS province.
play_reservoir_comment: The primary gas-productive formation in the Southern North Sea and in the application area in particular is the Permian Rotliegendes sandstone, these sandstones form the reservoir for all the discoveries and prospects identified within the application area. Multiple wells have penetrated the Rotliegendes sandstone in the SNS province.
play_seal_comment: The laterally extensive regional top seal for all identified field and prospects is the Zechstein Group evaporites. The thick deposits of evaporites, especially ductile halite which flows and reseals if faulted, along with tight interbedded carbonates form a regionally effective seal. Multiple wells have penetrated the Zechstein Group in the SNS province.

play_source_comment: The Westphailian coals have been exploited for Coal bed methane in Southwales during the industrial revolution. Hydrocarbon geochemistry has identified TOC of 60% and Vitrintite has suggested a maturity range of 0.5-3.0% with a kerogen type III within wells of the Southern North Sea. All Southern North Sea gas, to date, has been sourced from this interval.
play_reservoir_comment: Initial exploration within the Southern North Sea focused itself on the Rotliegendes Leman Sandstone in the 1960s; production initiated with the West Sole field and has since been producing. More recently, the discovery of the Cygnus field has extended the fault controlled northern limit of the fluvial Leman sandstone, draped upon the Mid North Sea High. The Rotliegendes Leman Sandstone has variable reservoir properties that can be characterised from poro/ perm relationships and facies associati
play_seal_comment: The Kupferschiefer has a consistent thickness of 30-60 cm within the Southern North Sea and is intersected by 2000+ wells and is the seal to the majority of gas fields. However there is places within the Southern North Sea where local reworking of the Zechstien transgression places the Z1 sequence unconformably upon the Rotliegendes group
source_presence_comment: Eldon is on the same latitude as Galahad and the clipper hub which is all charged from the sole pit to the North
source_effectiveness_comment: The prolific gas prone Westphalian coal measures, are proven and prominent throughout the Basin with a migration radius of ~15km
reservoir_presence_comment: Wells 48/13b-3 and 48/13b-8 intersected Rotliegendes Leman Sst.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Porosity within the 48/13b-8 well includes zones of poor porosity, sections of poor permeability may be overcome by hydraulic stimulation so is not seen as a risk
trap_presence_comment: De-keyser lineaments can be traced regionally through the seismic dataset, bounding faults have sufficient displacements.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The updip de-keyser lineament seals to the North, however there is uncertainty on the continuity of the seal along strike from these locations.

play_reservoir_comment: Jurassic sandstone encountered in 213/27-03z.
play_seal_comment: Lower Cretaceous shales present over Rosebank, similar geometry to this lead
source_presence_comment: Presence of Oil discoveries on the Corona and Rona Ridges.  Source rock is assumed to be from the Shetlands basin in this risking. Alternate models can charge this lead from the Faroes basin but source rock presence has yet to be proven.
source_effectiveness_comment: The offsetting Lochnagar discovery proves charge within the Jurassic section of the Corona Ridge. However, migration from the eastern Shetlands basin into the Glenfiddich lead can only be by complicated fill and spill mechanics.
reservoir_presence_comment: The offsetting 213/27-03z well penetrated a thick section of Jurassic sandstones of the Sule Skerry Formation. Adjacent Lochnagar discovery penetrated Rona Formation sands.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The age of the Jurassic sandstone present within this lead is uncertain.  The low reservoir quality of the Sule Skerry Formation sandstone makes reservoir effectiveness a risk.  Seismic data does not allow discernment between Rona and Sule Skerry Formation presence at this lead.
trap_presence_comment: 3-way faulted block present on seismic.  Weak seismic reflections show a dipping-down structural trend and off setting fault.  Overall seismic imaging is poor.
trap_effectiveness_comment: The overlying Cretaceous shales provide top seal and is proven at Lochnagar discovery. The eastern bounding fault is interpreted to juxtapose Jurassic reservoir against upper Cretaceous shales.

play_source_comment: Proven by wells. The Kimmeridge Clay has reached maturity for oil and gas generation in the Central Graben and provide the source of the oil and gas in all the neighbouring hydrocarbon discoveries.
play_reservoir_comment: Proven by wells. Also, the Mey Sandstone is the primary reservoir in the Orion field to the southwest, in Flyndre and Talbot to the east and in Joanne to the northeast.
play_seal_comment: Proven by wells and Mey fields; Orion, Flyndre, Talbot and Joanne.
source_presence_comment: World class Kimmeridge Clay Formation within late maturity window.
source_effectiveness_comment: Short vertical migration distance from underlying mature kitchen and oil proven in Talbot South discovery.
reservoir_presence_comment: Prospect is on the western edge of the Mey Sandstone fairway.  Reservoir is proven along the axis of the fan fairway to the southeast in the Orion field however the reservoir is missing from the 30/13-8 well on the Skerryvore diapir.  Seismic anomaly supports the presence of sandstone away from the well.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Where present, the Mey reservoir delivers at commercial rates even when relatively thin (Orion (4-5m).  Further helped by an expected fluid of light to volatile oil with a high GOR.  Slight risk to the reservoir deliverability when the reservoir is very thin at the pinch-out margins.
trap_presence_comment: Low relief structure with high structural complexity (stratigraphic trap).  Prospect defined by a moderate Lambda Rho anomaly.  Not visible on the far offset like the Skerryvore Mey prospect.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Mey sandstone encased in Lista Formation pelagic shales, which are proven effective in offset fields.  Lateral and up-dip pinch-out of the Mey is required which is supported by the lack of sand in the 30/13-8 well.  Some risk from leakage into underlying Lista debrites or an adjacent Mey Sandstone turbidite fan.

This is thought to be associated with salt movement at the time of deposition, which should not affect the Skerryvore North Mey area.  Seismic inversion data supports the presence of sandstone away from well 30/13-8 however no seismic attribute data is available over the prospect to de-risk reservoir presence.

play_source_comment: Proven by wells. The Kimmeridge Clay has reached maturity for oil and gas generation in the Central Graben and provide the source of the oil and gas in all the neighbouring hydrocarbon discoveries.
play_reservoir_comment: Proven by wells. The Chalk is a secondary reservoir in this area of the North Sea, although it forms a very important reservoir immediately to the southeast in the Orion and Affleck fields and east in Cawdor discovery.  Further to the east in the Norwegian North Sea the Chalk is a prolific fairway (Ekofisk, Eldfisk, Valhall etc.).
play_seal_comment: Chalk seals are proven effective by the numerous Chalk discoveries in the area (Cawdor, Flyndre, Orion). Tight Lwr Ekofisk Chalk is proven effective in Joanne.
source_presence_comment: World class Kimmeridge Clay Formation within late maturity window.
source_effectiveness_comment: Short vertical migration distance from underlying mature kitchen.  A deep-seated fault is seen to travel all the way from the Jurassic kitchen into the Skerryvore Tor prospect along strike.
reservoir_presence_comment: The porous Upper Tor zone is present in all offset wells.  The presence of a very convincing amplitude anomaly and seismically derived high porosity zone supports the fact that porous Tor reservoir is present in the prospect.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Tor reservoir generally requires natural fractures and/or acid stimulation to generate commercial flow rates as demonstrated by the Orion, Affleck and Joanne fields.  The predicted high porosities from the anomaly should ensure that better quality Tor reservoir is expected. However, the anomaly is not quite so bright as Skerryvore Tor therefore the porosities and permeabilities are expected to be slightly lower.
trap_presence_comment: Medium relief structure with high structural complexity (stratigraphic trap).  The presence of the trap (high porosity Tor surrounded by poorer quality Tor) is derived from a reliable amplitude anomaly.  However, the relief on the structure is less than Skerryvore Tor and the prospect is not covered by the inversion volume to further delineate the prospect outline.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Top seal is provided by tight Lwr Ekofisk Chalk proven effective in Joanne where the deeper Tor reservoir is separated from the Ekofisk.Basal seal is provided by either tight Lwr Tor or tight Hod,effective in the Affleck and Orion fields.The main risk is on lateral seal which is provided by a decrease in reservoir quality creating a strat trap and preventing hydrocarbons from escaping.This type of seal has not been proven in the offset fields but has been proven in the Danish sector-Halfdan.

play_reservoir_comment: Halley Alpha Discovery well, 30/12b-2 found an excellent quality Upper Fulmar reservoir 31m thick with a NTG of 74% and an average porosity and oil saturation of 25.2% and 82% respectively. The well tested at encouraging rates (11,276 bopd and 30.6 mmscfd).
play_seal_formation: Upper Jurassic Volgian (KCF) and Kimmeridgian (Heather Formation) shales/Lower Cretaceous Valhall and Cromer Knoll mudstones and marls
play_seal_comment: The Upper Jurassic Fulmar Sands and turbidite sandstones (Ribble and Jacqui Sandstones) are sealed vertically by deep-water Volgian (KCF) and Kimmeridgian (Heather Formation) shales. Where present, Lower Cretaceous Valhall and Cromer Knoll mudstones and marls will also act as an effective top seal. Top seal for Upper Jurassic reservoirs are proven effective at the Fulmar, Halley and Austen fields.

source_presence_comment: Regionally pervasive and proven by offset wells with multiple hydrocarbon accumulations at multiple stratigraphic levels. The Kimmeridge Clay Fm. has been proven a mature and viable source for established surrounding fields in the Mesozoic and Paleocene.
source_effectiveness_comment: Proven by HC migration into other Tertiary fields and discoveries in the NNS e.g. Nuggets. Vertical migration through faults and fractures from the Jurassic and Triassic reservoirs is evident in the form the gas chimneys on seismic sections and oil stains or shows in well cuttings throughout the Cretaceous and early Paleocene. Lateral migration routes through Paleocene sands are also visible on the spectral decomposition maps.
reservoir_presence_comment: The Asagao and Asagao North prospects exhibit clear differential compaction and channelised geometries, implying a high energy environment depositing unconsolidated, high porosity, sands.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Sand bypass and shale interbeds are also possible and may provide vertical and lateral compartmentalisation. Secondary mineralisation, particularly of glauconite, and other diagenetic processes may cause a reduction in porosity and permeability.
trap_presence_comment: A clear four-way dip closure exists across the Asagao prospect is clearly evident and is defined in both time and depth. A similar, but less regular, four-way dip closure also traps Asagao North. Some stratigraphic trapping may also be considered especially up-dip towards the shelf edge, where the sediment entry input point is located and a pinch-out geometry is assumed. A small NE-SW fault along Asagao?s SE edge may also provide a localised fault trap.
trap_effectiveness_comment: A regional and massive shale succession, in excess of 1000ft thickness, is present in 3/15-5 and 3/15-6 and can be seismically mapped and correlated between these two wells and over Asagao and Asagao North.
geophysical_cos_comment: SAAM DHI Boost of 44%

source_presence_comment: It is entirely likely that the Kimmeridge Clay Formation is present in the Wick Graben.  Given the structure of the area in the Jurassic a marked thickening compared to that seen  in the 12/14-1 well could be expected It also seems likely from regional mapping that it will  be at least partly mature. Other source rocks are also possible to charge the Baroosh  prospect such as the Devonian
source_effectiveness_comment: It is likely that the Burns Sands seen in the 12/14-1 well extend down into the Wick  Graben. If this is the case it is very likely that they wiil provide a pathway to migtrate  hydrocarbons towards Baroosh
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The Burns sandstone in well 12/14-1, which forms the downdip limit of the Baroosh  prospect is of excellent quality. Detailed seismic mapping has allowed the liekly extend of  the sandstone to be mapped. Given that the western limit of the Baroosh prospect is less  than 2km fro the 12/14-1 well it is very likely that sands will be encountered and that they  will be of good qulaity
trap_presence_comment: Top and Base sand ebvents tied to the 12/14-1 well have allowed for the identification of a  pinchout. This pinch out is consistent with the model for the sands derived from core  studies
trap_effectiveness_comment: Stratigraphic traps for the Burns sandstone are observed in other fields in the Inner Moray  Firth such as Buzzard and Golden Eagle. The stratigraphic element for this trap is not  towards the sediment input for the sands but rather represents the lateral limit of deposition  which has been mapped

Fluid quality is predicted to be poor (low API) due to biodegradation.
trap_presence_comment: The trap is defined as combination structural-stratigraphic which is reasonably well defined on 3D seismic. The up-dip fault edge shows significant offset and is well defined while the stratigraphic edge to the south-west carries more uncertainty. The stratigraphic pinch out extends far up the basin margin and the ultimate termination is not obvious in at least one area.
trap_effectiveness_comment: An effective seal at K80 level is present over most of the structure, but maybe compromised in the SW part of the lead where the K80 sealing shale thins and maybe onlaps near the ultimate crestal point.

source_presence_comment: Kimmeridge Clay Formation source rock proven in the basin by slope well 206/4-2. Extent and thickness of source rock outboard is uncertain, but likely to be sufficient.
source_effectiveness_comment: Spill from the Victory high is required to fill. Paleo-oil column interpreted in Victory wells but amount of spilled hydrocarbon is uncertain.
reservoir_presence_comment: Clair Group reservoir is proven in wells in back basin. Correlation of interval on 3D seismic into structure is uncertain but considered likely. Cretaceous reservoirs mapped on 3D seismic as bright, stripy interval developed unconformably overlying Clair Group.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: The AFTA and maturity work indicates that reservoir which is at shallow reservoir burial depths today was unlikely to have been significantly hotter in the past where pasteurisation could have occurred. A low API oil is now the reference case fluid. Reservoir deliverability risk is higher than at time of access and a critical risk for Voltaite.
trap_presence_comment: Described as a 2/3-way dip closed structure which is not well imaged everywhere but considered robust. The up-dip fault edge is reasonably defined on 3D seismic and obvious on gravity data. Degree of segmentation is uncertain
trap_effectiveness_comment: The seal modelled for Voltaite is the K80 flooding surface. This is calibrated to offset wells and present over the most part of the structure. The sequence becomes thin in the NE segment and there is some risk on presence and effectiveness. Fault seal against basement also carries some risk

source_presence_comment: Kimmeridge Clay Formation source rock is proven in the basin by slope well 206/4-2 to the south-west of Rustumite. Extent and thickness of source rock outboard is uncertain, but likely to be sufficient.
source_effectiveness_comment: Charge is predicted to come from the deeper basin via carrier systems that extend outboard of Rustumite via a relay ramp to north of the structure. This relay ramp could act as a barrier to charge, for example if it is heavily faulted or carrier systems are discontinuous across it.
reservoir_presence_comment: The most likely depositional setting for Rustumite is lobe deposition on a structured slope. A growth fault to the north-east creates accommodation for sediment accumulation. Sediments on the east of the structure likely sourced from the Shetland Platform whilst reservoir sands on the western part of the structure are more likely sourced directly from the partially emergent Rona High.
reservoir_effectiveness_comm: Deep burial and resultant high thermal exposure requires an effective porosity preserving mechanism to limit macroquartz overgrowth. The up-dip shelfal well 208/24-1a contains sponge spicules, which serve as a potential source for microquartz, and exhibits elevated porosity for the thermal history. However, the penetrated stratigraphy of this well is substantially shallower than the target interval at Rustumite and appears to exhibit less microquartz so the efficacy of this mechanism at Rustumite is uncertain.
trap_presence_comment: Stratigraphic trap with reservoir sandstones that wraps around the north-eastern nose of the Rona High. If the structure is filled, fault edges to the north-west and south-east constrain fluids, with a dip closure to the north-east. Seal capacity modelling these faults will only come into play in a max column height scenario. Reasonably well imaged on reprocessed seismic data designed to improve imaging at an important trap edge.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Rustumite reservoirs are most likely encased within slope mudstones acting as top and base seal. It is likely that igneous intrusions that are observed in the overburden crosscut reservoirs and potentially compromise top seal integrity.

play_source_comment: The marine and lacustrine shales which are interbedded with the reservoir unit, together with Westphalian coals, are the main source rocks. Source presence and maturity are proven by the nearby Fields and Discoveries (Kilmar, Kepler, Copernicus).
play_reservoir_comment: The Kinderscoutian sandstone reservoir is proven in the surrounding area and was a producing reservoir in the Kilmar Field to the south of the prospect.
play_seal_comment: The Carboniferous Westphalian shales and overlying Permian Silverpit shales and halite form the ultimate top seal for the play. The marine band (R. gracile) shale immediately overlying the reservoir is a proven topseal in the area.
source_effectiveness_comment: The Carboniferous source interval is mature in the AOI and proven by gas shows and columns in the adjacent wells. Migration into Bennett East via Bennett West provides a slightly higher risk.
reservoir_presence_comment: The Kinderscoutian sandstone reservoir package is present in the Cavendish Field immediately to the south of the prospect although quality is variable. High quality sandstones are seen in the Kepler and Copernicus wells to the southeast.
trap_presence_comment: Bennett West is dip-closed to the west with fault closure to the east whereas Bennett East is entirely fault-bounded. Fault seal from Cavendish north provides an additional element of risk in the high volumetric cases.
trap_effectiveness_comment: Nearby wells have topseal presence as proven by the successful test at Kepler although the thickness is variable and may affect the ability to hold a hydrocarbon column
